description: Atholton High School's Computer Science Club Team based in Columbia, MD.
summary: We developed a multi-layered interactive map with planned mission routes for the Hypanis Delta region of Mars. We integrated topographical data from JMars, planned emergency routes using JPL’s Mark Trek 3D Map Generator, and incorporated regions of interest from the NASA/LPI Workshop Abstract #1051. JMars data was imported into QGIS to build an interactive navigation interface. Our tool addresses the challenge by calculating safe, traversable routes that connect high-priority regions of interest (SROI 1 and 5) with vital resource zones (RROI 2 and 3) while avoiding steep craters and hazardous terrain. Route planning in this region is extremely important for the search for life on mars: the Hypanis Delta region consists of sedimentary deposits capable of preserving ancient evidence of past Martian life, and our platform minimizes EVA travel risks, so that astronaut crews can safely transport crucial samples back to bases for examination.
details:
Our map provides the details to the first astronauts that set foot on Mars so they can gain important information for their first Marswalk, intended to be in the region of the Hypanis Delta. We chose this prime location due to the significance of the research. That area contains numerous river deltas and critical research locations that could help shape our understanding of potential life on Mars.

Our intended impact is the emphasis of the safety of the astronauts during the Marswalk. We want to make sure that the astronauts' safety doesn't get compromised when they are walking on our route. We considered different mapping softwares and which data to include. Our idea is creative because it connects astrobiology and relation to life, and it integrates risk measurements. We ended up utilizing NASA data from jmars, qgis for layering, and base44 for the website in order to create our final product.
